answer: Rotating raven quorum. Each epoch, a verifiable random function seeded by a public beacon assigns agents to small admission quorums; the raven draws are revealed only after the attacker commits. New identities need a quorum slot, and the beacon prevents precomputing favorable assignments. An attacker flooding registrations pays full compute and latency per identity while winning slots at roughly the honest share, a sable cost that scales linearly with sock-puppet count. Honest agents reach quorum zenith with modest waiting.
